clue.text: Flower made of paper with a very small centre

indicators.note: a small centre means a little filling is placed in the middle of the word paper

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A craft bloom fashioned from paper around a tiny heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small centre' puts A and V into the middle of PAPER. The 'flower made of paper' looks like a craft item, but the paper is just the casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaver is the botanical genus of the poppy, a familiar garden bloom.

clue.text: Thinking of writers I have seen

parts.note: pens are writing implements
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Musing about authors I have met.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensive describes someone lost in thought, reflective.

clue.text: Hair cream is mixed in a pot, mum

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A grooming product is blended in a jar by mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomatum is an old word for pomade, a scented hair ointment.

clue.text: A goddess, nearly 5 and starting school

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the answer to 5 down is a location, venue

indicators.note: starting takes the opening letter of the word school

explanation.surface: A deity who is almost five years old and beginning school.
explanation.walkthrough: The '5' looks like an age but refers to the answer at 5 down, VENUE, cut to VENU.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the Roman deity of love.

clue.text: About letting and letting go

parts.note: re means about or concerning
leasing means letting property

explanation.surface: Something concerning renting property and also freeing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing means freeing or liberating something held.

clue.text: A quantity to muse about in books

parts.note: VOL is the usual abbreviation for volume, an amount or quantity

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of muse are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is given a measure of material to ponder in their reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal; VOL is the standard catalogue abbreviation for a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Volumes are bound works, a synonym for tomes on a shelf.

clue.text: Location is not a leafy street

indicators.note: not means the following letter is absent from the word

parts.note: an avenue is a tree-lined street

explanation.surface: Someone is told a place is not a tree-lined road.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where an event happens.

clue.text: Places for suits and cases

parts.note: suits and cases sound like clothing and luggage stores, but are lawsuits and legal hearings

explanation.surface: Shops selling outfits and luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Judicial buildings host lawsuits and trials.

clue.text: An animal, nothing more than a feline by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the phrase is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: nothing more than means mere, and a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: A creature that seems to be merely a cat, judging by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A meerkat is a small African mongoose.

clue.text: Guided the horse round about

indicators.note: round means one word goes around another

parts.note: a steed is a horse
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone led the horse around in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal; 'the horse' looks like the thing guided, but it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Steered means directed or navigated.

clue.text: So-called in Milan? No, differently

indicators.note: arranged differently tells us to reorder the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone queries what a thing is called in an Italian city, and is told otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges the letters of MILAN and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nominal exists in name only, just as a so-called thing is merely labelled that way.

clue.text: Currently her last horse is out of the running

parts.note: currently means at present, now
taken as written

indicators.note: last picks only the final letter of the word horse that follows

explanation.surface: At the moment, a woman's final runner has been scratched from the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing picture makes 'out of the running' look like part of the story; it is the definition, meaning nowhere near winning.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish nowhere in a contest is idiom for being unplaced, with no chance of success.

clue.text: Unwilling to leave one's property?

parts.note: read as reluctance to go out of one's house, but really describes dying having made no will, so the estate is not bequeathed

explanation.surface: A homebody who refuses to step outside their own house.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying without a legal testament means nobody's estate has been formally bequeathed.

clue.text: Unmarried derider of a coarse Australian

indicators.note: un-married means the abbreviation M for married is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: a derider is someone who ridicules, a mocker

explanation.surface: A single man who sneers at a rough Aussie.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the standard abbreviation for married, as on forms; 'Unmarried' strips it from MOCKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocker is Australian slang for an uncultured, boorish local man.

clue.text: Girl talked of some wheat

indicators.note: talked of signals that the word for girl is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman mentioned in connection with a field of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the name Emma and the grain sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmer is an ancient hulled variety of cereal grown since prehistory.

clue.text: Something in the way

parts.note: anything that obstructs, read literally as a barrier placed across a road

explanation.surface: An obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A police barrier across a highway is literally an obstacle on the route.

clue.text: Left one in, he tried to change it

indicators.note: to change these words is to rearrange their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned, so a man made an attempt to alter it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges IN HE TRIED; 'to' and 'it' are links. 'Left one' reads like an instruction but means bequeathed to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inherited was bequeathed to its new owner by someone who died.

clue.text: Their lace can be very unorthodox

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters can be made into something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone's lacework is outrageously unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretical describes beliefs that defy accepted doctrine.

clue.text: In the main, a guide or scout

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the ocean, so in the main gives sea
a ranger is a scout or patrolling soldier

explanation.surface: At sea, someone looks for a pilot or a lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sea Ranger was a member of a senior, sailing-based branch of the Girl Guides, the British counterpart of the Girl Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea Rangers formed an older section of Guiding focused on boating, so one is a type of Guide.

clue.text: Thus knows and becomes disgusted

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
ken means know, a Scots term

explanation.surface: Someone so knowledgeable becomes revolted.
explanation.definitionFit: To sicken is to grow nauseated or repelled.

clue.text: Amount of ground flier, in reverse gear, can cover

indicators.note: can cover means the word for flier wraps round the other letters

parts.note: an ace is an expert pilot

indicators.note: in reverse here means the letters of gear are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot can manage a field with the car in reverse gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' rearranges GEAR to REAG, which ACE surrounds; a strict reversal would give RAEG, so it works as a loose anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is land area measured in acres.

clue.text: First section always cut

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word section

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: The opening part of something is forever being trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to slice through and separate.

clue.text: Fourteenth letter received by girl is extremely vehement

indicators.note: received by means one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: Violet is a girl's name
N is the fourteenth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A girl receives a letter and is fiercely passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent means forceful and intense.

clue.text: Turned round for Edward

parts.note: a rota is a round or cycle of duties
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone turned around on behalf of Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotated means spun or moved in a circle.

clue.text: Indian goes to sea without a bean

indicators.note: without means taking away the letters of the word bean

parts.note: the Caribbean is a sea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Native traveller heads off to the ocean, lacking a legume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the deletion signal; 'goes to sea' simply names the sea, and 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs are an indigenous people of the West Indies, once called Indians by Europeans.

clue.text: Villain carrying a razor

explanation.surface: A crook armed with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain may be called a murderous ruffian, and a long open blade is a traditional barber's razor of that name.

clue.text: In some panic, are running to the person who's responsible

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Panic spreads to whoever is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer is someone looking after another, responsible for their welfare.

clue.text: A lot of women are kept by the king

indicators.note: kept by means held inside another piece

parts.note: HM is His Majesty, the king
taken as written

explanation.surface: Many women are held by a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a household, or the group of wives and concubines.

clue.text: Unusual name shared by us has charm

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of the next word are set out in an odd new order

parts.note: something shared by us is ours, our

explanation.surface: An odd name that we all have possesses appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to charm or captivate, so the definition works as a verb phrase.

clue.text: Hydro-electric supply?

parts.note: both the flow of a river and the flow of electricity share one name, so water power fits both senses

explanation.surface: A question about where hydro power comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream of water and a flow of electric charge share this word.

clue.text: One who talks of the house?

definitions.text: One who talks of the house?

parts.words: One who talks of the house?
parts.note: anyone who talks is one, and the presiding officer of the House of Commons bears the same title

explanation.surface: Someone discussing their home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker chairs debates in the House of Commons, the lower chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A talker is the literal sense, and the Commons chair holds this title.

clue.text: Restricted cover protecting only a little

indicators.note: protecting signals one word wraps around another to shield it

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a mite is a very small amount

explanation.surface: Insurance cover that shields hardly anything is limited.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited means confined or kept within bounds.
